final.answer: The description does not show how FT-12-2 is actually configured, so I cannot say whether its fail-state output is driven high or low in this plant. What the documents do say (for the HART 4-20 mA output, code A): if self-diagnostics detect a sensor or microprocessor failure, the analog signal is driven either high or low to alert the user, and the failure mode selection — high or low failure — is user-selectable with a jumper/switch on the transmitter. So to change the alarm direction, move the internal jumper/switch on the transmitter; note that the actual alarm levels depend on whether it is configured to standard, NAMUR-compliant, or custom levels (e.g., NAMUR low ≤3.6 mA / high ≥22.5 mA, default low ≤3.75 mA / high ≥21.75 mA).

Note that no separately orderable item is explicitly named a 'seal kit' — the closest equivalent is the wear-part set 2.

final.answer: Control loop FIC-14-1 operates control valve FV-14-1, a Fisher ET globe valve. Its datasheet lists several trim options: standard trims (e.g. trims 1, 4, 27, 28, 29, 29C, 37, 37H, 57, 85, 85C, 87, 87C), Whisper Trim I / Whisper Trim III / Whisper NXG Trim / WhisperFlo noise-attenuating cages, Cavitrol III cavitation-protection cages, and a Trim Cartridge option. For high pressure drop or noise, the Whisper trims (Whisper Trim I, Whisper Trim III, Whisper NXG and WhisperFlo cages) provide aerodynamic noise attenuation, while Cavitrol III cages provide cavitation protection under high pressure drop; the datasheet distinguishes between these two purposes rather than naming a single trim for both.

final.answer: FV-14-1 is described by an ET/EAT/ETR valve datasheet that offers flanged ends, not just buttweld or screwed. The available end connections include RF or RTJ flanged CL150, CL300 and CL600 (for carbon/alloy/stainless steel bodies), CL125 FF and CL250 RF flanged (for cast iron bodies), plus PN flanged ratings (PN16 to 40, PN63 to 100), alongside butt weld, socket weld and screwed options. So yes, it can be supplied with flanged ends.

final.answer: GV-11-2 is a solenoid valve (a Type 165 2/2-way servo-controlled diaphragm solenoid valve), so yes, it needs electrical power to operate. The documentation for it lists available supply voltage options of 24V DC, 230V AC (50/60 Hz) and 115V AC (50/60 Hz), with matching coil-set order codes for each, so the valve is offered in multiple voltage variants. The description does not record which voltage variant this specific valve instance was ordered with, but both 24 V DC and 230 V AC are supported variants, so 24 V DC will work if the valve is fitted with the 24V DC coil; otherwise you would need the 230V AC coil version. Also note it runs on AC or DC depending on variant, with power consumption of about 5 W (DC) or 11 VA operation / 20 VA inrush (AC).

final.answer: Yes, 2 1/2 is a port size, but not the only one: P-1-3 is a 4" x 2 1/2" (102 mm x 64 mm) pump with raised face flanges. Per the datasheet's dimension drawing, the suction connection is the larger 4-inch flange (8 bolt holes on a 7.50 in bolt circle) and the discharge is the smaller 2 1/2-inch flange (4 holes on a 5.50 in bolt circle); optional 4.00-8 NPT and 2.50-8 NPT companion flanges are available. Note the datasheet states the size as 4" x 2 1/2" overall and does not explicitly say in words which port is which — that assignment comes from the dimension drawing.

final.answer: For FV-12-2, the available body materials are cast iron, WCC carbon steel, LCC carbon steel, WC9 chrome moly steel, CF8M (cast 316 stainless steel), CF3M (cast 316L stainless steel), or other materials upon request (with CD3MN also listed). Its datasheet lists these seal materials for the valve plug seal (Table 14, pages 20-21): carbon-filled PTFE (2-piece seal, standard for NPS 1-6 valves without Cavitrol III cage) rated -73 °C/-100 °F to 232 °C/450 °F; ethylene-propylene rated -40 °C/-40 °F to 232 °C/450 °F (not for petroleum-based fluids and hydrocarbons); fluorocarbon rated -18 °C/0 °F to 204 °C/400 °F (not for steam or ammonia, not for water above 82 °C/180 °F); nitrile rated -40 °C/-40 °F to 71 °C/160 °F for air and hydrocarbons (or up to 82 °C/180 °F for other compatible fluids; not with fire-resistant hydraulic oils); PTFE with N10276 spring (spring-loaded seal, standard for NPS 8 valves and NPS 1-6 valves with Cavitrol III cages) rated -73 °C/-100 °F to 232 °C/450 °F; and PTFE/graphite with R30003 spring plus PEEK anti-extrusion rings rated -73 °C/-100 °F to 316 °C/600 °F, but limited to 260 °C/500 °F in oxidizing service. The metal parts (backup/retaining rings, springs, S41600 stainless parts, PEEK rings) are described as not limiting for temperature, except the S41600 stainless parts of the spring-loaded seal, which have a minimum of -29 °C/-20 °F. A part literally called a piston ring does not appear in the datasheet; the closest items are the plug seal rings and the PEEK anti-extrusion rings.

However, the description shows no block (isolation) valves and no drain or vent around TV-15-2; the only valve on its upstream side is the check valve CHV-15-2, and per standard P&ID practice a check valve without a screw-down stop is not suitable for isolation. final.answer: Cavitation is possible because reduced flow and noise can be consistent with it, but the P&ID and available datasheet information cannot confirm the cause. No single NPSHr or operating flow is specified, so the required NPSH cannot be stated; it depends on the pump’s NPSH curve at the actual operating flow, which is not provided.

Datasheet fisher-et-d100022x012, pages [4, 3, 2, 7, 25]:
This valve can have all three flow characteristics — quick-opening, linear, or equal percentage — depending on which cage is installed.

Details from the datasheet (Table 1. Specifications, pages 3–4):

- **Standard Cages**: quick-opening, linear, or equal percentage [p. 3, also p. 4]. The easy-e Valve Family page confirms this: "Standard cage flow characteristics: quick-opening, linear or equal percentage" [p. 2].
- **Whisper Trim, WhisperFlo, and Cavitrol Cages**: linear only [p. 3, also p. 4].

So the valve is not limited to one characteristic: with standard cages you can choose any of the three, while with the Whisper Trim, WhisperFlo, and Cavitrol (noise/anti-cavitation) cage options, only the linear characteristic is available. Which trim cartridge variants are offered also reflects this — the Trim Cartridge table (Table 5, page 7) lists "Equal Percent, Linear" as available characteristics for the ET variant.

(These terms describe how the flow through the valve changes as it opens: "linear" means flow changes in step with opening, "equal percentage" means each equal step of opening gives the same percentage change in flow, and "quick-opening" means flow rises very fast at the start of opening.)

score.reason: All three with standard cages; the special cages are linear only.

trace.content: Consider the transmitter that feeds controller FIC-12-2. When the transmitter fails, does the output go high or low, and how do I change that alarm direction?
{"tool": "drawing", "question": "Which transmitter feeds controller FIC-12-2?"}

Tool result:
{"answer": "The transmitter FT-12-2 feeds controller FIC-12-2; the diagram shows FT-12-2 sending a process signal to FIC-12-2.", "not_present": false}
{"tool": "datasheet", "tag": "FT-12-2", "question": "On transmitter failure, does the output signal go high or low? Can the failure direction (alarm direction) be configured or changed, and how?"}

Tool result:
Datasheet rosemount-3051-00813-0100-4001, pages [88, 110, 26, 42, 74, 15, 52, 63]:
Yes – on failure the analog output is driven either high or low, and you can choose the direction yourself: for HART 4-20 mA output, "High or low failure mode is user-selectable with a jumper/switch on the transmitter" [p. 88]. For the 1-5 V low-power output (code M), the high or low alarm signal is user-selectable by an internal jumper [p. 88].

Details (all from p. 88):

**When it happens (HART 4-20 mA, output option code A):** if self-diagnostics detect a sensor or microprocessor failure, the analog signal is driven high or low to alert the user.

**How high or low the signal goes depends on the alarm setting (Table 5, "Failure mode alarm", p. 88):**
- Default setting: high alarm ≥ 21.75 mA, low alarm ≤ 3.75 mA. (Note: the High Alarm default is ≥ 22.5 mA for some options – codes M6, DA1, T9, RK.)
- NAMUR-compliant setting (option codes C4 or CN): high alarm ≥ 22.5 mA, low alarm ≤ 3.6 mA.
- Custom levels: high alarm 20.2–23.0 mA, low alarm 3.6–3.8 mA. (Note: low alarm must be 0.1 mA less than low saturation, and high alarm 0.1 mA greater than high saturation.)

**For the 1-5 Vdc low-power output (code M):** on a gross transmitter failure the signal is driven either below 0.94 V (low alarm) or above 5.4 V (high alarm); which one is set by an internal jumper.

**For digital outputs (codes F, W, X – e.g. Fieldbus/wireless):** no high/low drive; a gross failure is passed as an alert and a status along with the process variable. Accordingly, the alarm-level options are only available with HART 4-20 mA output (code A) and do not apply to Fieldbus, PROFIBUS PA, or wireless [p. 88, p. 109].

**Leakage (shutoff) classes** – Table 4 on page 6 lists shutoff classes per ANSI/FCI 70-2 and IEC 60534-4 (industry standards for how much a valve leaks when shut) by valve design and seating type:
- Class IV is standard for metal seating (all constructions except Cavitrol III cages), [p. 6]
- Class V is optional with metal seating (requires spring-loaded seal ring, radius-seat plug and wide-bevel seat ring; not available with 8-in. port, quick-opening cage, or trims 4, 29 and 85), [p. 6]
- Class V and VI are optional with PTFE seating (Class VI per Table 6), [p. 6]
- Class V with metal seating also applies to ET valves with Cavitrol III one- and two-stage cages, [p. 6]
- For ET and EAT valves with TSO ("Tight Shutoff") trim (CL125 through 600): TSO is not an ANSI/FCI leakage class; these valves are factory tested to a more stringent Emerson requirement of no leakage at time of shipment, with water as the test medium (specify service P when ordering). Shutoff class is V. [p. 6]

**Class VI availability and seat load** – ET valves with soft seat or metal seat can provide ANSI/FCI Class VI shut-off. Table 6 on page 7 shows Class VI is available for port sizes 3.4375–7 in., not for NPS 8, with limited retrofit capability (consult your Emerson sales office). Minimum seat load (the force pressing the plug against the seat, which affects leakage): 300 lbs/lineal inch for metal seat; for soft seat, see Catalog 14. [p. 7]

**Seat ring / plug seal description** – The datasheet describes the seating and plug seal parts:
- Standard seating is metal-to-PTFE seating (for stringent shutoff requirements) in all valves except Cavitrol III cages; metal-to-metal seating is optional for all other valves [p. 2]

Yes — all three of those types are available, plus a few more.

trace.content: Regarding GV-11-2 on the P&ID: Does it need power? If so, what voltage, and will 24 V DC work, or do I need 230 V AC?
{"tool": "datasheet", "tag": "GV-11-2", "question": "Does this valve need electrical power? What voltage/power supply is required (e.g. 24 V DC or 230 V AC)?"}

Tool result:
Datasheet gfps-165-solenoid-valve, pages [2, 5, 4, 1]:
Yes, this solenoid valve needs electrical power – it is an electrically operated 2/2-way solenoid valve with different voltage variants. The datasheet lists these supply voltages: 24V DC, 230V 50Hz/60Hz and 115V 50Hz/60Hz, with a voltage tolerance of ±10 % [p. 2].

Details you need:

- Supply voltage options: 24V DC, 230V 50Hz/60Hz, 115V 50Hz/60Hz [p. 2, "Specifications"]. Note: a "solenoid" is the electric coil that opens/closes the valve, so power is always required to operate it.
- The valve comes in variants with AC (alternating current, e.g. mains supply) or DC (direct current, e.g. 24V supply). Available variants by nominal diameter (DN = pipe size):
  - DN 15, 20, 25, 32, 40, 50: available in both AC and DC versions [p. 2]
  - The exact voltage and current type for your valve is given on its type plate – the datasheet says: "Observe the voltage and type of current as given on the type plate" [p. 4, Electrical connection].
- Order variants also exist by gasket material (EPDM or FKM) with supply voltage 24V DC, 110V AC or 230V AC [p. 2 / order tables].
- Power consumption while operating: 5 W (DC versions) and 11 VA (AC versions) for all sizes DN 15–DN 50; AC versions also have an inrush power (brief higher draw at switch-on) of 20 VA [p. 2, "Kv 100 values" table].
- Voltage tolerance: ±10 % – the supply may deviate by this much [p. 2 and p. 4].
- Connection is via a cable plug (appliance plug, DIN EN 175301-803 form A, included in delivery), protection rating IP65 (dust-tight and protected against water jets) [p. 2 and p. 4].

score.reason: Lists the 24 V DC/230 V/115 V versions and says to match the type plate.

Datasheet fisher-et-d100022x012, pages [20, 21, 2]:
The valve plug seal (the seal ring that sits around the plug) comes in several materials, and their usable temperature ranges are listed in Table 14, "Materials and Temperature Limits for Other Parts" [p. 20]. The metal parts of the seal (backup ring, retaining ring, spring) are stainless steels that the table says are "not limiting factors" for temperature — the soft seal material is what sets the limit:

- **Fluorocarbon** (same part group): –18 °C / 0 °F to 204 °C / 400 °F. Meant for high-temperature air, hydrocarbons and certain chemicals/solvents; not for steam or ammonia, and not recommended for water above 82 °C / 180 °F [p. 20]

- **PTFE with N10276 spring** (spring-loaded valve plug seal, standard for NPS 8 valves and all NPS 1–6 valves with Cavitrol III cages): –73 °C / –100 °F to 232 °C / 450 °F [p. 20]
- **PTFE/graphite with R30003 spring** (spring-loaded valve plug seal with PEEK anti-extrusion rings): –73 °C / –100 °F to 316 °C / 600 °F, but only up to 260 °C / 500 °F in oxidizing service (oxidizing service means contact with hot air/oxygen-containing media) [p. 20, also p. 21]

A few related points from the same table:

- The PEEK (PolyEtherEtherKetone) anti-extrusion rings used with spring-loaded seals are listed as "not limiting factors" for temperature [p. 20]. The General Application section on page 2 gives an extended temperature (ET) limit with PEEK anti-extrusion rings of 316 °C / 600 °F in non-oxidizing service and 260 °C / 500 °F in oxidizing service [p. 2].
- The S41600 stainless steel parts of the spring-loaded seal have a minimum of –29 °C / –20 °F, and these parts are not used with ports of 137 mm / 7 in. or larger [p. 20].
- For gaskets: the N04400/PTFE gasket runs –73 °C / –100 °F to 149 °C / 300 °F; spiral-wound gaskets are not limiting [p. 20].

The table is organized by part group, so check the row for your valve size and cage type (2-piece seal vs spring-loaded seal) to pick the right material. Datasheet rosemount-3051-00813-0100-4001, pages [10, 22, 3, 70, 39, 52, 18, 5]:
Yes — the transmitter offers DA1 diagnostics. DA1 is the option code for "Loop Integrity and Plugged Impulse Line diagnostics" under Plantweb™ diagnostic functionality, which detect issues that might compromise the integrity of the output signal [p. 5, p. 10].

About the low-power 1-5 V output (output code M):

- DA1 is available with both the 4-20 mA HART output (code A) and the low-power output (code M) [p. 10].
- However, per footnote 2: **with the low-power output code, only the Plugged Impulse Line Diagnostic is included** — the Loop Integrity diagnostic is not [p. 10].

So: with the low-power 1-5 V option, both diagnostics are listed under DA1, but in practice only the Plugged Impulse Line diagnostic is included; Loop Integrity requires the 4-20 mA HART output (code A) [p. 10].

For background: the Plugged Impulse Line diagnostic continuously monitors for plugged impulse lines and alerts on abnormal conditions, while the Loop Integrity diagnostic monitors the electrical loop for issues such as corrosion, water in the housing, or an unstable power supply [p. 3]. Diagnostic events are tracked in a built-in diagnostic log [p. 3].

Note: the footnotes giving these output-code restrictions appear in the ordering tables for the 3051C (p. 10), 3051T (p. 22), 3051CFA (p. 39), 3051CFC (p. 52), and 3051L (p. 70).
